properties.areaDesc: North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 27 at 1:31AM PST until November 29 at 5:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.7 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along San Pablo and San Francisco
Bays.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at
12:31 PM Friday, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM
Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM
Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 27 at 1:31AM PST until November 28 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.7 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft.

* WHERE...The Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Saturday
morning. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at
12:31 PM Friday, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM
Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM
Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Visibility of 1 SM or less with visibilities decreasing to
less than 1/4 SM overnight.

* WHERE...North Bay Interior Valleys.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Low visibility could make driving conditions hazardous.
properties.instruction:
If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of
distance ahead of you.
